adversarialChallenges.challenge: You first wrote coverageAnswer() class-gated (each field carried only on the class that owns it) and then DROPPED the gating in favour of forwarding whatever the upstream sent. Is that not a loss of discipline — a stray outOfCoverageCounty riding on a no-hit would now reach the wire?
adversarialChallenges.answer: The gating was removed deliberately, and it is the narrower rule. legacy-design-tools ALREADY gates by construction (routes/brokeragePlaceSitusSearch.ts carries each field only behind its own truthiness guard) and its own test asserts no cross-contamination ('does not attach outOfCoverageState to a plain no-hit'). A second gate here would be a second implementation of an upstream rule, and its only observable effect would be to hide an upstream contradiction instead of showing it. Nothing downstream can misread the pass-through: coverageMissFromWire reads the block regardless of class, and coverageMissSentence only uses the county on county_out_of_coverage and only uses the state on out_of_coverage. What IS refused is a MALFORMED block (a county with no countyName), which the customer could not read anyway — asserted.

adversarialChallenges.challenge: A timeout from cortex used to leave this BFF as a 502/503. It now leaves as HTTP 200. Anything that alerts on 5xx from /api/pe-situs-search stops firing on a cortex outage. You have removed a machine-readable outage signal to make the customer message nicer.
adversarialChallenges.answer: This is a real trade, and it is the one the dispatch asks for by name (item 4: 'A timeout must read as "coverage check unavailable", never as a miss'). The mitigation is that the status is not the only signal: `missClass: 'coverage_check_unavailable'` plus a reason naming the failure ('cortex responded 503', 'cortex timed out after 9000ms', 'cortex fetch failed — socket hang up') is a MORE specific signal than a bare 502, and the four probe subjects for P-205 cannot see it otherwise — surface-probe.mjs grades a body carrying `error` as UNMEASURED, so the old shape was invisible to the instrument that is supposed to page on it. I could not verify whether any deployed alert rule keys on this BFF's non-200 status (no monitoring config lives in this repo), so it is named in the CLOSE as a leave_behind for the integration seat rather than claimed as safe.

adversarialChallenges.challenge: 9 seconds is a long time to wait for a typeahead. You made the dropdown slower for every customer on the coverage path.
adversarialChallenges.answer: The alternative is worse and was the actual bug: at 5s the ceiling sat ~1.2s above the measured 3.8s path (Cameron, 2026-09-18), so a slow-but-answering coverage check was reported to the customer as an outage. The 9s ceiling only elapses when cortex is not answering; it is not added latency on the answering path. It is also bounded by the instrument: the probe's own budget for this leg is 12s, so 9s keeps a genuinely-too-low ceiling MEASURABLE. The residual is named rather than hidden: a full-ladder miss is slow in the typeahead (250ms debounce, then the coverage path), which CP1 already recorded as an open thread and is not this lane's to fix.

adversarialChallenges.challenge: Your fall-through stop keys on two literal class strings. If cortex adds a fifth out-of-coverage class, a geocoded pin stands in for it again and no test fails.
adversarialChallenges.answer: True, and it is the honest limit of the rule. It is not silent, though: COVERAGE_MISS_CLASSES and isOutOfCoverage are the ONE place the rule lives, and a fifth class would land in the unrecognised-class path, which renders 'the parcel search could not answer for that address just now' rather than a covered miss — asserted for both a real unrecognised class and a synthetic future one. Since the four names are read at source from cortex's own union (txgioAddressResolve.ts line 1179), a fifth class is an upstream change that arrives with its own lane.

adversarialChallenges.challenge: The customer-leg probe grades the four subjects, and NONE of the four exercises your variant-precedence rule or the timeout path. Part of your change is unfalsifiable by the instrument that will grade the row.
adversarialChallenges.answer: Correct, and that is why two files exist: situs-search-client.test.ts pins the precedence rule (and pins the fact that each of the four subjects produces exactly ONE situs variant, so the probe cannot reach the rule at all), and pe-situs-search-route.test.ts drives the real handler's timeout path with fake timers. Both were run against the reverted source too. Neither is a substitute for the probe; both cover what the probe structurally cannot.

adversarialChallenges.challenge: The raw-Find path suppresses the error line for a quiet lookup (search-landing's `runParcelLookup(query, { quiet: true })`), so a picked address that misses shows a chip, not your sentence. Is the class still reaching 'the Find box' in that path?
adversarialChallenges.answer: Partly, and it is declared rather than papered over. The quiet path is the DROPDOWN-PICK path, and for the two out-of-coverage classes the dropdown no longer offers a pickable address row at all — it shows the sentence in place of the rows — so the quiet path is not the first reading the customer gets. When a pick does miss, the pre-existing OUTSIDE_COVERAGE_CHIP from search-landing.ts (P-270's surface, a different file this lane does not touch) is what shows. Changing that chip to carry the class would mean editing search-landing.ts, which is in flight for another lane; it is named in leave_behind.
